concept: BottomNav prints the phone app's main sections along the bottom edge of the case like the scale under a radio's dial, glyph over word, with one ink index mark under the section you are in.

default_to_avoid.pattern: Material bottom navigation with a pill-shaped active indicator behind a filled icon
default_to_avoid.why_not: A tinted pill is a second surface language and a filled icon is a loud mark; P1 keeps selections out of colour and P5 keeps printing flat.

default_to_avoid.pattern: iOS tab bar with a blue tinted current icon and label
default_to_avoid.why_not: A blue tint is colour alone telling the place, and P5 asks for ink on plastic with no tinted text.

references.source: Braun RT 20 table radio (Dieter Rams, 1961): band names printed in one row on the case, the chosen one marked by an index
Braun SK 4 radio-phonograph (Hans Gugelot and Dieter Rams, 1956): one printed scale, one pointer
WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices, Landmark navigation and aria-current=page for the link to the page being shown

derivation.consequence: labels sit on the body's inset line, never floating mid-surface
derivation.form: The section words sit on one printed line along the bottom edge of the strip, each glyph straight above its word.

derivation.consequence: one grotesk, regular and medium only; hierarchy by size and position
derivation.form: The current section is set in medium weight and the others in regular, at the label size, with no size jump.

derivation.consequence: links, borders, icons, selections and charts never use it
derivation.form: The current section is told by weight and one ink index mark under its word, never by orange or a tinted fill.

derivation.consequence: every part keeps ≥44px hit area even when it draws smaller
derivation.form: Each link is a full quarter of the strip and at least the control.lg height, though the glyph draws at twenty pixels.

derivation.consequence: fixed positions, so a unit's layout does not reflow between states
derivation.form: A hidden medium-weight copy of each word holds its width, so moving between sections never shifts a neighbour.

options.name: printed index, glyph over word on the bottom strip with Tabs' ink mark; a printed side index rail on wide screens
key bank, four raised capsule station keys with the current one latched low
mode window, a recessed LCD strip with the current word lit and the others ghosted

variants.reason: A is printing on the case like Tabs and the book's side index, so the sections stay quiet beside each unit's one orange control (P1, P5); B adds four raised keys that compete with every unit's loud control, and C turns navigation into a second display whose ghost words read as disabled (P2).

root.why: The strip is the bottom edge of the case, a plastic band with the section words printed on its inset line.

fixed.why: Fixed to the bottom of the screen, the strip keeps one place on every page of the app.

auto.why: The layout follows the screen, so a tall phone gets the bottom strip and a wide screen the printed rail.

rail.why: On a wide screen the words are printed down the inline start like an index, each glyph beside its word.

list.why: The links share the strip in equal parts so each word sits on the same printed line.

link.why: Each link fills its share of the strip and stands at least the control.lg height for the thumb.

glyph.why: The glyph is printed with the two pixel stroke, flat on the plastic, never filled or embossed.

word.why: The word stacks a hidden medium copy under the visible one so its width never changes with the weight.

text.why: The visible word is set at the label size in regular weight, the printing on the case.

ghost.why: The hidden medium copy reserves the widest form of the word so neighbours keep their places.

mark.why: The index mark is ink at full step on the chosen section only, never orange, like the mark on Tabs.

hover.why: Hover only darkens the word's ink one step, because printing does not rise when a finger comes near.

aria-current=page.why: The section being shown is set in medium weight with the ink mark under it, told by weight and mark together.

focus-visible.why: Keyboard focus draws the shared focus ring around the whole link so the target shows where it is.

@media orientation: landscape.why: On a screen wider than it is tall, auto turns the strip into a rail at the inline start, an index down the edge.

@media prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.why: The ink fade moves nothing, so it stays under reduced motion just as on Tabs.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the strip keeps a real border and the mark takes the link text colour so it survives.

color.why: Only the word's ink changes on hover, over motion.hover, so nothing travels or swells.
